name: Animal disease response
description: Foreign animal disease response for exercises: premises designations and the zones they sit in, movement permits, sampling schedules, depopulation and disposal, indemnity, and the notices producers, exhibitors and consumers receive. Rules are tagged with the response plan edition they come from. Disease dynamics, epidemic curves and tracing come from the epidemiology toolkit. Stays at coordination level: no pathogen handling detail, fictional premises only.
outsideParties: USDA APHIS Veterinary Services (area veterinarian in charge, national reference laboratory)
the state animal health office and state veterinarian
the integrator or cooperative and its contract growers
county emergency management and the sheriff (checkpoints)
the state or county health department (worker health)
haulers, rendering and disposal site operators
the county fair board and extension

glossary.definition: Infected (IP), contact (CP), suspect (SP), at-risk (ARP), monitored (MP), free (FP); vaccinated (VP) is secondary. Only an at-risk premises can become monitored.

Infected zone around an infected premises; buffer zone beyond it; both are the control area. The surveillance zone lies outside it, in the free area. Vaccination zones are containment (inside) or protection (outside).
Infected zone 3 km; buffer zone 7 km beyond; control area at least 10 km from the closest infected premises; surveillance zone at least 10 km wide. Epidemiology may widen them.

A network laboratory result; the national reference laboratory confirms. Plan clocks start at the presumptive result. HPAI Red Book (May 2017): after the index case, presumptive positives inside an established control area may be acted on without waiting for confirmation; those outside it go to the reference laboratory.
Goal: depopulation within 24 hours of the presumptive positive; with limited crews, the premises with the most potential for spread go first.
Contact premises every 5 days for 14 days; at-risk and monitored every 10 days, and surveillance zone premises every 21 days, until 56 days after the last case.

productConventions: Premises are a code and a fictional farm name; never a real farm, owner or address.
State the plan and edition beside any distance or interval, and say the state plan governs.
Counts, distances and times match across the order, permit, letter and press release.
realismRules: Do not move a premises to monitored unless it was at-risk.
A presumptive result comes from a network laboratory before the reference laboratory confirms.
Unaffected producers keep working under permit; do not close a whole sector without a stated reason.

Dairy movement rules changed in 2025 and 2026; the designer confirms current state rules. HPAI in dairy cattle is handled by herd quarantine and testing, not by the poultry zone minimums or depopulation.

criticalTasks: Set up a unified command with the federal veterinary service and state the objectives for each operational period.
Quarantine premises and set the control area and surveillance zone from the plan minimums, recording the basis for any change.
Request federal resources and an emergency declaration with a stated reason.
Keep one designation for each premises across the tracing, laboratory and permit teams.
Issue producer, exhibitor and consumer notices with the same counts, distances and times as the control area order.
Answer the food safety question for consumers in the first message.
Correct a wrong zone or a wrong farm named in a post.
Keep the premises list, designations and the curve of confirmed premises in agreement.
Track laboratory turnaround and the presumptive and confirmed results separately.
Report sampling due and sampled by designation.
Decide movement permits within the service target, with testing and conditions.
Keep unaffected producers moving product under permit and explain each denial.
Tell trading partners the zone and dates.
Depopulate infected premises against the 24 hour goal, ordering premises by potential for spread when crews are limited.
Choose a disposal site and method with capacity and travel checked.
Monitor the health of workers exposed to infected animals.
